as_of_note: Quarterly prints are the research-dashboard snapshot as of Jul 2026. Next-report dates that the 9 Sep sync had already moved are shown as reported, not as still ahead. Not Act. Not a score.
lead: The money is going into the spenders' capex, not into a new ticket. That spend is a tailwind for the quality already held, and a cash drag on the companies writing the cheques. Do not add Tesla on the robotaxi spend. Paper stays hold.
watch: Hyperscaler AI capex for 2026, as printed on this snapshot: Google $180–190B, Amazon ~$200B, Microsoft ~$190B, Meta $125–145B. Tailwind for the compute and power names. Free-cash-flow drag on the spenders.
Strategic buildouts on the same snapshot: Palo Alto–CyberArk/Chronosphere ($25B), GE Vernova–Prolec ($5.3B), Rocket Lab Neutron, Tesla's $3B Texas chip plant, Constellation–Calpine ($21.8B).

quarterly.caption: Most recent reported quarter on the Jul 2026 snapshot. Calendar-Q2 season had not started yet on that print, except names that report on a fiscal spring. ETFs and crypto are omitted. They do not report earnings.

Orders more than doubled. Backlog $176B. FY26 revenue guide raised to $45.5–46.5B. Wind orders –40%.
Backlog $2.2B +108%. Neutron medium-lift was on track for a later-2026 debut on that print.
Calpine close and 920MW of new nuclear PPAs. FY26 adj EPS guide raised to $11.50–12.50.
